h1: The 7 Best Quiet NAS for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Quiet Home Office NAS 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven NAS options for quiet home offices, from the 2-bay Synology DS223 to a single-bay Buffalo, plus advice on bays and drives.
summary: The Synology DS223 is our top pick because its home-and-office focus and overnight task scheduling suit a desk you sit beside. The Beelink ME Pro is the quietest-by-design option, built around a low-power mini PC and SSD slots. The Buffalo LinkStation is the simplest, with a drive already inside.
intro: A NAS is quiet only when it is idle, and the noise people hate comes from drives spinning up and fans ramping during a transfer. No listing here publishes a decibel figure, so anyone promising a measured number is guessing.

We ranked seven storage boxes on the things that actually decide noise in a home office: bay count, whether you can run on SSDs, cooling design, how fast transfers finish, and whether you can schedule heavy work for the night. These are design signals from the spec sheets, not sound readings. We left out the QNAP TR-004 because it is direct-attached storage, not a network NAS.

products.name: Synology DS223 Home & Office Backup Hub (2-Bay Diskless NAS)
products.verdict: Mature software and overnight scheduling for a desk-side box.
products.description:
The DS223 is a two-bay, diskless NAS running Synology's DSM software. It handles file centralization, backup and monitoring, supports scheduled overnight tasks, and is aimed at homes and small offices. It costs $200 to $500.

Scheduling heavy jobs overnight is the practical quiet trick, since drives work hardest when you are away. It tops the list because that software maturity matters more than raw hardware for a box you live next to.

Buy it for steady daily backup. The caveat is that its noise depends on the drives you fit, because none ship in the box.
products.idealFor: A desk-side backup box run mostly overnight.

products.name: Beelink Mini PC ME Pro, 2 Hard Drive Bays NAS
products.verdict: A low-power mini PC with three SSD slots for silent storage.
products.description:
This is a mini PC with an Intel N95 processor, 12GB of memory and a 128GB M.2 SSD, plus two hard drive bays, three M.2 SSD slots and dual LAN. It works as a file server, NAS or private cloud, and costs $200 to $500.

SSDs have no moving parts, so filling its M.2 slots is the closest thing to a silent NAS in this group, and the low-power design generates less heat. It ranks below the Synology because the software is less NAS-specific.

Choose it if silence beats capacity. The caveat is that SSD capacity costs more per terabyte than hard drives.
products.idealFor: People who put silence ahead of capacity.
products.skipIf: You want a polished NAS operating system.

products.name: TERRAMASTER F2-425 2-Bay NAS Storage
products.verdict: Quicker transfers mean the drives spend less time working.
products.description:
A two-bay, diskless NAS with an Intel quad-core x86 processor, 4GB of RAM and a 2.5GbE port, capable of multimedia serving. It sits at $200 to $500.

Speed helps with noise indirectly, since a faster network wraps up a big copy sooner and the box returns to idle. It ranks third because that benefit only appears if your router supports 2.5GbE.

Pick it for large file moves. The caveat is that listing says nothing on noise.
products.idealFor: Large file transfers that finish quickly.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP2800, 2-Bay for Content Creators
products.verdict: Cooling designed for sustained load, which can mean steadier fans.
products.description:
A compact two-bay desktop NAS, diskless, aimed at content creators, with cooling designed for sustained load stability and the UGREEN NAS OS ecosystem. It costs $200 to $500.

Steady cooling can mean a fan that holds one tone rather than surging, which many people find less irritating. It ranks fourth since the listing gives no sound figures to confirm that.

Best for creators moving big files. The caveat is that it is more NAS than a quiet office needs.

products.name: Asustor Drivestor 2 Gen 2 AS1202T, 2-Bay NAS
products.verdict: A lower-cost box that suits light, quiet backup duty.
products.description:
A two-bay diskless NAS with a quad-core 1.7GHz processor, 1GB of DDR4 RAM, a 2.5GbE port and 4K media server support. It costs $100 to $200.

Its modest hardware suits backup better than constant video work, and heavy transcoding is what makes a NAS loud. It ranks fifth because it has the least memory of the 2-bay group.

A fit for budget offices that only back up. The caveat is the 1GB of RAM.
products.skipIf: You stream and transcode a lot.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DH2300, 2-Bay Desktop NAS (Diskless)
products.verdict: Plain two-bay storage with no creator extras.
products.description:
A diskless two-bay desktop NAS supporting up to 64TB, running UGREEN NAS OS with a focus on simple backup and file sharing. It costs $100 to $200.

Without creator-grade hardware, it asks less of its fans during ordinary file serving. It ranks sixth because the listing is sparse and nothing sets it apart from the Asustor.

Buy it for plain file sharing. The caveat is limited headroom.
products.skipIf: You want extra services or speed.

products.name: BUFFALO LinkStation 210 2TB, 1-Bay NAS (Drives Included)
products.verdict: A one-bay box with a 2TB drive already inside.
products.description:
A single-bay NAS with a 2TB drive included, offering home cloud storage, basic file sharing and backup. It costs $100 to $200.

One drive means one source of spin noise, and not having to buy a drive removes the biggest decision. It ranks last because one bay offers no redundancy.

Choose it for the easiest start. The caveat is a single drive, so a failure loses your copy.
products.idealFor: A first NAS with minimal setup.

methodology.title: Transfer speed
methodology.description: Faster networking finishes copies sooner, shortening noisy periods.

methodology.title: Fit for backup duty
methodology.description: Light backup duty is quieter than constant transcoding, so we matched hardware to role.

methodology.title: Price fit
methodology.description: Each pick was weighed against its price range.

whatMatters.detail: Hard drives spin and click, while SSDs make no mechanical noise. A NAS with SSD slots can be near silent. Check for M.2 or SSD slots.
Each bay adds a drive and its noise. One or two bays keep sound down. Check the bay number in the title.
Constant video transcoding makes fans ramp. Backup and file sharing are lighter. Match the hardware to your actual jobs.
Moving heavy tasks overnight keeps noise away from working hours. Look for scheduling features in the software.
None of these listings publish decibels. Treat quiet claims as design hints and check owner feedback. Never trust an unsourced dB number.

howToChoose.intro: There are three ways to keep a NAS quiet.

Synology DS223, Beelink ME Pro, TERRAMASTER F2-425, UGREEN DXP2800

cards.label: SSD
cards.text: No moving parts and near silent, but costlier per terabyte. The Beelink ME Pro is the pick.

cards.label: Hard drive
cards.text: Cheap capacity but audible. The Synology DS223 and others use drive bays.

howToChoose.note: Most home offices should default to hard drives with overnight scheduling, unless silence is critical.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Compact size, few bays and the option to run SSDs.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Beelink ME Pro and the single-bay BUFFALO are the smallest sound sources.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Silence matters. The Beelink ME Pro supports SSDs and the Synology DS223 schedules overnight.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The NAS can sit in a closet. The Asustor or UGREEN DH2300 is enough.

faq.q: Are any of these truly silent?
faq.a: Only an SSD-based setup comes close, such as the Beelink ME Pro with M.2 drives. Hard drive models always make some sound.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with a quiet NAS?
faq.a: Trusting a quiet claim with no data. None of these listings publish decibels.
Indirectly, since faster transfers end sooner. It needs matching network gear.
Only the BUFFALO LinkStation 210 lists a 2TB drive included. The rest are diskless.

faq.q: How do I schedule overnight tasks?
faq.a: The Synology DS223 supports scheduled overnight tasks in its software. Check settings for backup and maintenance timing.

faq.q: Why not a USB storage box?
faq.a: A direct-attached unit like the QNAP TR-004 is not network-attached, so we left it out.

finalTake: The Synology DS223 is the best quiet NAS here because overnight scheduling keeps drive noise out of working hours. The Beelink ME Pro is the choice if you will go all SSD. The BUFFALO LinkStation 210 is a simple, drive-included starter.
